I.          INTRODUCTION
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
1.4       In so far as the subject of Sports is concerned, this figures in the State List of the Constitution. In view of this, it is
the State Governments who are primarily responsible for the development and promotion of sports. The Ministry of Youth
Affairs & Sports in its effort to complement the State’s efforts aims at development of a broad based sports culture
throughout the country, and significantly expanding the pool of talented sportspersons who can be groomed to bring
laurels to the country in international events. With this in view, a major initiative proposed to be launched by the Ministry
is a scheme with the title ‘Panchayat Yuva Khel Abhiyan’, which is aimed at creating basic sports infrastructure, and
promoting sports activities at the village/sub-district level, both as a necessary ingredient of youth development and as a
means to substantially widen the catchment for spotting of talent.  The Committee desires that Panchayat Yuva Khel
Abhiyan should be finalized at the earliest and the details in this regard may be furnished to the Committee.  
 
Action Taken
 
            The scheme of Panchayat Yuva Krida Aur Khel Abhiyan (PYKKA) has been approved in principle by Planning
Commission.
 
            Necessary action for the preparation of EFC proposal has been initiated.  A copy of the PYKKA proposal is placed
at Annex-I.
 
 
II.        BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
2.12     The problem of pending UCs with NGOs, the Committee notes has seen no visible improvement; it, in fact,
appears to be increasing in some schemes. The NGOs that have outstanding UCs need to be blacklisted and the good ones
must be encouraged to come forward in a big way.
 
Action Taken
 
             With a view to streamlining the procedure and bringing in uniformity across the 4 NGO related grants-in-aid
schemes, it was decided to implement the revised procedure w.e.f. 2006-07.  Instructions in this regard were issued to all
the State Governments/UT Administrations dated 1 May 2006. According to this revised procedure, the Ministry is to
invite applications from NGOs after giving advertisement in the newspapers.  The recommending authorities in the
districts are to forward NGOs applications in duplicate to the Secretary (Youth Affairs) in their respective State
Government/UT Administrations after verifications of their antecedents and countersigning the application.  The State
Government/UT Administrations are to constitute a State/UT Level Screening Committee (SLSC) under the Chairmanship
of the Secretary (Youth Affairs) in the State/UT for screening, scrutiny, pre-appraisal, technical feasibility etc. of these
proposals.  The SLSC are to examine the proposals on the basis of technical capability, availability of infrastructure,
trained manpower for the proposed activity and past performance/credibility of the NGO including their financial
soundness, non-involvement in the anti-social or anti-national activities.  The SLSC are to shortlist a limited number of
proposals and prioritize before they are forwarded by the State Government in a single copy to the Government of India
scheme wise.
 
            This revised procedure adopted in 2005-06 has resulted in getting better quality proposals and also much lesser in
number (in hundreds in place of in thousands). The priority accorded by the State/UT was strictly followed so as to avoid
any discretion. Since States/UTs were involved in the forwarding they were also requested to monitor and provide
assistance wherever needed in making the programmes success. As a result between 60-70% of the grantees sanctioned in
2005-06 came back for 2
nd installment within the year itself. The ministry has taken a proactive step of reminding the
remaining NGOs who have not submitted UCs so far.
 
With effect from current financial year i.e. 2007-08 the following measures have been taken to further streamline the

IV        NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN
 
Recommendations/Observations
4.9       Due to Ministry’s decision not to open new Youth Clubs/Mahila Mandals, the Committee notes, position in these
States/UTs listed above would remain the same. Now, in view of putting the opening of new Clubs/Mandals on hold in
2007-08, the position is not going to improve. The Committee feels that instead of taking a decision not to open new
Clubs/Mandals at the national level, at least these deficient States should have been taken up during 2007-08. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the expansion of these Clubs/Mandals be taken in these States for 2007-08 itself
and additional funds for this purpose be provided.
 
Action Taken
The recommendation of the Committee is noted for necessary action. It may also be noted by the Hon’ble
Committee that the Minister for Youth Affairs & Sports has directed NYKS to mobilize youth and ensure that there is at
least one club in each village in the North Eastern States.
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
4.12     The Committee has been further informed that in the context of the 11
th Five Year Plan, it is proposed to bring in a
paradigm shift in the manner of funding and implementation of the programmes by NYKS. In the 11 th Five Year Plan the
Youth Clubs are proposed to be made the main executing agency of the programmes in the villages. In this context the
NYKS has initiated a process of categorization of Youth Clubs into ‘A’ (Very Active), ‘B’ (Active) and ‘C’ (Dormant)
categories. It is proposed that the Youth Clubs under ‘A’ and ‘B’ categories comprising about 25%  of the total number of
Youth Clubs in the country will be provided direct funding to carry out youth related programmes at a village/cluster level,
while the District Kendras will focus their efforts on activation of the other clubs and certain identified core activities. It is
expected that these changes in the approach will enhance not only the participation in the programmes but also lead to
activation of the youth and the youth organizations in general. The Committee expresses its reservations about the
proposed direct funding to A & B category Clubs. The Committee would like to have more details in this regard. The
Committee is perturbed to see that only 25% of the total number of (2.5 lakh) Youth Clubs deserves to be under ‘A’ & ‘B’
categories. It is really disturbing to note that 75% of the Youth Clubs are not in proper shape particularly when large part
of the NYKS budget was being appropriated for their development. The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry
should have been more diligent in ensuring proper development of Youth Clubs. The Committee recommends that NYKS
should evolve effective strategies to ensure proper development of Youth Clubs and also put in place an effective
monitoring mechanism over them.
 
Action Taken
 There has been a rethinking about the classification of youth clubs into A,B & C categories. The criteria for
classification of youth clubs has since under gone a change from the current financial year with the introduction of the
concept of achieving synergy between youth/social issues and sports and games.  In order to achieve this objective Block/
Sub District Level Campaigns are proposed to be launched for Youth Club mobilization, activation, strengthening and
development of self sustaining/ self reliant Youth Clubs.  As indicated in reply to the question 4.7 above the clubs will be
expected to achieve concrete results in the way of beneficiaries and only such clubs who can achieve synergy between

without verifying their antecedents and reputation.

4.18     The recruitment process to the post of District Youth Coordinators was cancelled by the competent authority on the
grounds inter alia that the posts had not been sanctioned by the Ministry of Finance; a number of complaints had been
received about the recruitment process. Some of the applicants had also moved to the Court against the non-declaration of
the result due to cancellation of the recruitment process. The Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in its Order dated 03.3.1999
directed the respondents to declare the results of the examination and stated that, if the petitioners are found successful,
they should be appointed. On appeal, this order was set aside by the two-judge bench of the same court on 02.8.2000 and

4.19     The Committee would like the Ministry to make all efforts for an early settlement of the case. The Committee
would like to state that whenever the recruitment process is restarted, the candidates of the impugned recruitment process
should be given preference.
 
Action Taken(Paras 4.18 & 4.19)
 
            Director General NYKS has moved an application for an early hearing of the case. Necessary action would be
taken as and when the judgment is delivered.
 
VI        PROMOTION OF NATIONAL INTEGRATION PROGRAMME
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
6.4       It is given to understand that the procedure is being streamlined and the guidelines revised. The Committee would
like to know about these guidelines and their implementation.
 
Action Taken
 
The guidelines for streamlining the procedure for various youth schemes including Scheme of Promotion of
National Integration had been issued in May 2006. As per the guidelines, the proposals of the NGOs / Volunteers
Associations are to be routed through the State Govt duly recommended and prioritized.  The State Govt. will constitute a
committee named State Level Screening Committee for proper screening and scrutiny. Thereafter State Govt. will forward
the proposal to the Ministry according to the priority for sanction of financial assistance to NGOs. 
 
VII      NATIONAL SERVICE VOLUNTEERS SCHEME
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
7.4       The Scheme aims at deploying 4400 NSVs during 2007-08. Under the scheme, the volunteers are enrolled in the
beginning of the year and allotted to Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan and National Service Scheme. The recruitment is
made by a District level Committee headed by the collectors.
 
7.5       The Committee notes that there is a little awareness about the existence of such a scheme in the public. The

Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan publicizes about the deployment of National Service Volunteers through affiliated
youth clubs/mahila mandals only. Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports provide funds for publicity of the scheme, by giving
advertisement in both National and Local media.  
 
VIII     YOUTH HOSTELS
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
8.2       The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation for Youth Hostels has decreased to Rs.1.25 crore in BE 2007-08
in comparison to Rs.3.50 crore allocated in RE 2006-07. This reduction has been made in view of lower actual expenditure
till September, 2006 under Youth Hostel scheme.  The Committee notes with concern the continuously low utilization of
funds under this scheme. Against an allocation of Rs.4.50 crore in 2005-06, the Ministry could utilize only 1.49 crore.
Further in 2006-07, against an allocation of Rs.3.50 crore, the Ministry could spend a mere Rs. 7 lakh only till 31.12.2006.
The extremely low utilization of funds has severely affected the construction of Youth Hostels. The Committee is
perturbed over such a poor performance of an important scheme from its inception. It recommends the Ministry to make
effort to improve the situation and devise specific measures to address various problems associated with this scheme.
 
Action Taken
 
            It may be clarified that during the year 2005-06, an expenditure of Rs.1.05 crores was incurred under the Scheme
upto June, 2005.  The expenditure was Rs.2.45 crores upto September 2005 and Rs.3.84 crore upto December, 2005. 
Thereafter, a total of Rs.4.28 crores was spent upto March, 2006.  Ministry has utilized the funds of Rs.4.28 crores (and
not Rs.1.49 crore) against an allocation of Rs.4.50 crores during 2005-06.  Hence, it would not be correct to say that
utilization of funds were extremely low during 2005-06.  Similarly, during the year 2006-07, against an allocation of
Rs.3.50 crore, the Ministry had spent Rs.2.27 crores till 31.12.2006 and Rs.2.77 crores upto March, 2007.
 
            As regards improving the situation, Ministry has been writing to the State Governments and CPWD from time to
time to expedite the construction work.  As already stated, Ministry has taken remedial action for improvement in the
system by stopping release of approved funds still the identified sites are fully developed and handed over to CPWD for
construction.  After taking over of developed land, CPWD is requested to intimate the date by which the construction work
will be started and on receipt of their specific reply intimating schedule of construction, this Ministry initiates action for
release of approved funds.  These funds are released in suitable instalments to ensure its expeditious utilization which also
avoids any possibility of idling away of funds with CPWD.
 
            Also, the projects under construction are regularly reviewed /monitored with the Secretaries/Directors (Youth
Affairs & Sports) of the State Govts.   With all these steps, it is observed that the pace of construction has improved
considerably which has resulted in completion of four more Youth Hostels at Rewari(Haryana), Badrinath (Uttaranchal),
Khajuraho(Madhya Pradesh) and Sogalu (Karnataka).  Two other Youth Hostels viz. K.A. Peta at Vizianagaram and
Cuddapah in Andhra Pradesh which were included in the list of ‘under construction projects’, are now near completion. 
Construction in hostels at Churachandpur and Thoubal in Manipur is also in full swing.  The focus of this Ministry is now
on the on-going projects only.  Since the funds are limited, it is difficult to meet the demands in respect of all projects, at a
particular time.
 
Recommendations/Observations
 
8.5       The Committee’s attention is drawn to the oft-repeated fact that failure to get a developed site from the State
Government is the main reason behind the delay. However, the Committee has been informed that approval is given and
the funds under the scheme is released only after examining a developed site which is handed over to the CPWD for
construction of Youth Hostels. If it were so, the Committee fails to appreciate the problem of late or non-availability of
requisite site for the Hostels. In this backdrop, the Committee desires the Ministry to furnish a note as to the factors that
have caused delay in construction of Youth Hostels, since such delays result in time and cost overruns.

Recommendations/Observations
9.3       The Committee is not happy at the unspent balance becoming a recurring feature in the SAI. The underutilization
of Plan funds must have affected various programmes/schemes being run by SAI for promotion of sports in the country.
The Committee feels that this also must have hindered the attainment of excellence in various sports. The Committee
strongly recommends the Ministry to ensure that SAI utilizes the Plan funds completely on time and in the proper manner.
 
Action Taken
 
            During the year 2006-07 close monitoring through out the year has resulted into optimum utilization of the
allocated funds and there has been an increasing trend in the utilization of the allocated funds.  Against the total allocation
of Rs.135.25 crores, total expenditure during the year 2006-07 is Rs.136.76 crores, which is 101.12% of the approved
allocation. Instructions have been issued by SAI Head Qtr. to all the Units/Regional Centres of SAI to ensure optimum
utilization of allocated funds during the year 2007-08. To ensure   full utilization of allocated funds by SAI Ministry has
been pursuing SAI vigorously.   In this regards, a monthly meeting with the Executive Director (Finance) and other
officers/ officials from SAI has been fixed to discuss and monitor the activities of SAI. As a result, grants released to SAI
in the first quarter of the current financial year have been fully utilized.
 
Recommendations/Observations
9.7       The Committee feels that the existing system of financial management in the SAI is weak and that needs to be
strengthened. It has been the experience of the Committee that due to inadequate supervision/monitoring of the financial
affairs, instances of irregularities as well as adverse audit reports have been reported during the recent years. The officials
looking after finance in the SAI are either over-burdened or are given responsibilities about which they do not have
relevant experience. As a result, they are not able to spare required time for their main responsibility. In view of the above,
the Committee feels that the person looking after finance should be given other responsibilities only when they are able to
fulfil their primary responsibility in an effective and comprehensive manner.
 
Action Taken
 
The accounting system of the SAI has been improving since last financial year (2006-07).  The organization was
able to utilize 100% grants that were provided by the Ministry in 2006-07.  All the new initiatives approved by the SAI
Finance Committee and the Governing Body have been taken up and good progress has been made in all the infrastructure
projects like laying of synthetic surfaces, sports hostels and provision of new infrastructures in various SAI centres.
